newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian insurer Balta heads to bourse.
newsitem.headline: Latvian insurer Balta heads to bourse.

text.p: Leading Latvian insurance company Balta is to start an issue of new shares on July 7, the first stage in its becoming a quoted company, Trasta Bank, arranging the issue, said on Wednesday.
Balta will be the first company on the bourse that is not a former state-owned firm.

"The fact that Balta is becoming a public company is a significant event because just now all the companies on the bourse are companies that have been publicly privatised," Trasta said in a statement.
The bank is arranging the issue of 200,000 shares or 6.5 percent of Balta's share capital at 1.75 lats each.
Balta intends to apply for a bourse listing after August 22 when it has finished placing its shares with investors.
It also said it hoped its shares would reach 2.5 to three lats by the end of the year.
Balta had a 282,341 lats first quarter profit against 423,000 lats profit for the whole of 1996.
The company is the market leader in vehicle, agriculture and real estate insurance.
